newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentine storms block wheat exports to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine storms block wheat exports to Brazil.

text.p: Brazilian wheat millers are facing an accute supply shortage as storms and high seas in the Argentine port of Necochea block shipments of wheat, said the Brazilian Association of Wheat Industries (Abitrigo).
"There are around 33 vessels queued up to load in Necochea which has been having problems for 30 days with storms and high seas," said Abitrigo president Antenor Barros Leal.
"There are some (Brazilian) mills which have already stopped and various mills are in a difficult position," he said. Ten of Brazil's 200 mills were paralyzed by the shortage, he added.
Necochea ships some 100,000 tonnes of wheat per week and there is currently a two-and-a-half week delay in shipments, Leal said.

Most mills usually have a stock of one month but since the government introduced limits on the financing of imports earlier this year, many have reduced their stocks to between 10 days and two weeks, he said.
"The law resulted in people buying less wheat so stocks were low when this problem hit us," Leal said.

Brazil has already imported 2.3 million tonnes of wheat this year, of which 2.2 million were from Argentina, he estimated. He forecast total 1997 wheat imports at 6.0 million tonnes, of which 4.5 million tonnes were seen coming from Argentina.
If supply problems persist, millers will ask the government to liberate imports from the United States, currently prohibited from entering the country because of phytosanitary regulations.
"One option is to import from the U.S.," Leal said. "We will ask the government to liberate these imports."
